chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
Regarding a person in ihram who slaughters a bird, indeed upon him is the blood of a sheep which he must pay. If it is a chick, then a young goat or a small lamb from the sheep.
And that which indicates that it is incumbent upon him is the value of the egg, one dirham, when he is in ihram.

key_terms.دَمَ شَاةٍ: The blood compensation, specifically a sheep or its equivalent value
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: A person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation (dam) for slaughtering a bird while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar details the specific fidya for slaughtering birds while in ihram, distinguishing between a chick (compensated by a young goat or lamb) and an egg (compensated by one dirham). It reflects the juristic methodology of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in categorizing compensation based on the developmental stage of the bird, providing practical guidance for pilgrims. The ruling underscores the precision required in fulfilling ritual obligations during Hajj and Umrah.
